  This express Brazil tour combines 3 nights in Rio de Janeiro and 2 nights near Iguazú Falls. ## Rio de Janeiro and Iguazú in 6 days: who is this express tour for?

**Six days and five nights** are enough to combine the panoramas of [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) with both sides of Iguazú Falls if you do not have time for a longer journey. The route is aimed primarily at travelers ready for active sightseeing days: mountain viewpoints, city neighborhoods, a flight and several walking routes around the falls.

The program includes **3 nights in Rio and 2 in Foz do Iguaçu**. Day one is for arrival, day two for Sugarloaf Mountain, day three for Corcovado and Rocinha. Day four combines a domestic flight with the Brazilian side of the falls, day five is for the Argentine side and day six involves the return flight connection. Days 3–5 are especially busy, so this format suits travelers who value a packed schedule.

## What you can see in Rio

Day two includes a **four-hour group excursion with an English-speaking guide**. The route begins at [Praia Vermelha](/brazil/place/praia-vermelha/), after which a cable car takes you over Urca Mountain to Sugarloaf. From the viewpoints, you can see how the bay, ocean beaches and residential districts fit among the rocky peaks.

Day three has two separate group excursions of approximately four hours each. In the morning, you visit Corcovado, Christ the Redeemer and the city panorama. After lunch, the program introduces Rocinha. A visit to a residential neighborhood differs from a trip to tourist viewpoints: follow your guide's instructions, respect residents' privacy and comply with local expectations.

This schedule leaves less free time by the ocean than a journey with several beach days. Travelers wanting to spend unhurried time on Copacabana and Ipanema should compare other [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/).

## How the Brazilian and Argentine sides of Iguazú differ

On day four, after arriving in [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), you visit the Brazilian side of the falls. This is an excellent place to appreciate the broad front of cascades as a single panorama. Walkways and viewpoints lie at varying distances from the water, and spray sometimes reaches visitors.

Day five takes place on the Argentine side, reached by crossing the border towards [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Trails and viewpoints offer closer looks at individual falls from other directions; a highlight is Devil's Throat. Trail access may change with strong currents, rainfall and national park operations.

A key feature is that **both sides of Iguazú are already included**, rather than offered as alternatives. Crossing into Argentina, however, means entry requirements must be checked for each traveler's nationality. For some visitors, documents rather than walking distances are the main practical consideration.

## How flights and transfers work

The tour begins with a transfer from Rio Airport to the hotel. Day four includes a drive to the airport, a domestic flight towards Iguazú and a transfer after arrival. On day six, there is a private airport transfer after hotel checkout, then a flight via Rio or São Paulo to connect with an international departure.

**The domestic flight is listed as a separately charged service arranged on request.** It must not be counted automatically in the base tour price. When choosing tickets, allow enough time for connections and confirm that the selected arrival time permits the Brazilian falls excursion on day four.

Different service formats apply: **Rio excursions are shared group trips with an English-speaking guide**, while airport transfers are provided with a driver. The word "private" describing a transfer does not mean every excursion is private.

## Included services, price and alternatives

The tour price is **$2110**. It includes hotels with breakfast, scheduled excursions and airport–hotel–airport transfers with a driver. International and domestic flights, additional excursions, food and drinks during transfers are listed separately. Compare trip costs together with the necessary air arrangements.

This tour concentrates on two main areas: the city and the falls. If you have more time and want to add the Amazon and the ocean coast, consider the [11-day Exotic Carnival itinerary](/brazil/tour/brazil-exotic-carnival-champions-parade/). For nature-focused journeys, explore [Brazil wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Rio–Iguazú express tour

### How many nights are spent in each place?

The program includes 3 nights in Rio and 2 in Foz do Iguaçu, for a total of 6 days and 5 nights.

### Do we see the waterfalls from both sides?

Yes. Day four covers the Brazilian side and day five the Argentine side. Crossing the border requires appropriate documents.

### Are the Rio excursions private?

No. Sugarloaf, Corcovado and Rocinha are visited on group excursions with an English-speaking guide. Private transfers are a separate type of service.

### Are flights between Rio and Iguazú included?

The domestic flight is listed among exclusions and can be arranged on request. International flights are also excluded.

### Is this a relaxed beach holiday?

Most of the trip is devoted to excursions and transfers. For an extended stay by the coast, choose another itinerary with several free days.

## A 13-day private Brazil tour: five distinct experiences in one journey

This [private Brazil tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-iguazu-pantanal-bonito-buzios-private-tour/) lasts **13 days and 12 nights**. The route combines [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), both sides of Iguazú Falls, the [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/), [Bonito](/brazil/place/bonito/) and [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/). It brings together a Carnival event, nature excursions and a free day at the beach.

The main difference from a shorter Rio and Iguazú trip is the combination of five regions offering very different experiences. Covering this much geography takes time: domestic flights, transfers and several changes of hotel are necessary. The trip suits travelers wanting to explore Brazil's different natural environments in one journey and comfortable with a busy schedule.

## How the 13 days are divided by region

| Stage | What happens |
|---|---|
| Days 1–3 | Rio, city panoramas and the Champions Parade |
| Days 4–6 | Both sides of Iguazú |
| Days 7–8 | Nature excursions in the Pantanal |
| Days 9–10 | Bonito, caves and waterfalls |
| Days 11–13 | Búzios and return to Rio |

These are not five separate day trips from one hotel. You must move between bases several times. A short beach stage at the end offers a chance to rest after early starts in the natural areas, but it is significantly shorter than on the dedicated [Carnival tour with seven nights in Angra](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-carnival-angra-dos-reis-12-days/).

## Rio and the Champions Parade: the calendar determines the start

The Rio program includes a cable car ride to Sugarloaf, an excursion to Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado and **the Champions Parade at the Sambadrome**. The Champions Parade is different from the main competitive processions: it is a celebratory performance by the best samba schools after the Carnival results are announced.

Departure dates have not yet been fixed. Before arranging flights, the most important check is whether the trip dates match the **Champions Parade itself**, not just any Carnival procession. The previous year's schedule cannot simply be reused for a later trip. Admission to the Carnival event and hotel–Sambadrome–hotel transfers are included.

To compare journeys centered on Carnival, see our [events and festivals selection](/interests/events-and-festivals/).

## Iguazú: why there are two days

After Rio, the route continues to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The Brazilian side gives broad views of the system of cascades. On the Argentine side, visitors explore upper and lower walking trails and approach Devil's Throat from another part of the gorge. These excursions reveal different aspects of the same natural attraction; replacing one with the other means missing part of the experience.

The falls lie on the border of two countries. Even when the tour is sold as a journey through Brazil, one excursion day takes place in Argentina. Entry, transit and return requirements must be checked for each traveler's nationality. Some trail sections may be restricted when water levels rise, so access should be checked closer to the visit.

## The Pantanal and Bonito: two different nature experiences

The [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/) is a region of wetlands, pools and seasonal flooding. Observing birds and other wild animals in their natural habitat is central here. The program focuses on nature excursions, including early departures; sightings of any particular animal species can never be guaranteed.

The rainy and dry seasons significantly affect travel conditions. During drier months, animals may be more noticeable near remaining pools; in wetter months, road access and available routes depend on water and local conditions. Because this tour is tied to a Carnival event, **the Pantanal season cannot be chosen independently**, and safari expectations need to be aligned with Carnival dates.

[Bonito](/brazil/place/bonito/) offers another type of nature holiday: clear rivers, limestone caves and swimming in designated natural areas. The itinerary mentions the [Blue Lake Cave](/brazil/place/blue-lake-cave-bonito/), Rio Sucuri and the [Mimoso River waterfalls](/brazil/place/mimoso-river-waterfalls/) in the Estancia Mimosa area. Visiting Blue Lake Cave means exploring a natural monument; unrestricted swimming in its underground lake is not part of the standard excursion.

The distinction is useful when choosing: in the Pantanal, the primary activity is watching wildlife; in Bonito, it is walking and joining water activities in a karst landscape. Check each operator's rules, available times and medical restrictions for river activities in advance.

## Included services and guide languages

We organize hotel accommodation with breakfast, transfers and excursions. **Russian-speaking guides accompany guests in Rio and Iguazú; English-speaking guides work in the Pantanal and Bonito.** This matters if Russian-language assistance in every region is important to you.

Carnival tickets and Sambadrome transfers are included. **International and domestic flights are paid separately**, with a preliminary budget estimate for domestic flights. Additional excursions and meals beyond the specified amount are also charged separately. Compare the exact included services and final timetable with your chosen travel dates.

The route involves several airports and natural regions, so allow enough time between flights and transfers. For the Pantanal and Bonito, light long-sleeved clothing and protection against sun, insects and moisture are useful. Wear nonslip shoes for the Iguazú trails.

## Búzios at the end: why a free day is included

In [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/), travelers have time to rest beside the ocean after the sightseeing stages. You can spend the day on a beach or choose extra marine activities. The resort stay is short: it is the final stage, not a week-long beach holiday.

If an extended beach break after Carnival matters more, compare the [12-day Rio and Angra dos Reis itinerary](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-carnival-angra-dos-reis-12-days/). For waterfalls, caves and other natural landscapes, see [Brazil nature itineraries](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/). For planned birdwatching and wildlife encounters, there is a separate [wildlife tour selection](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/).

## Frequently asked questions about the private Rio–Pantanal–Bonito tour

### Is it suitable for a relaxed beach holiday?

It is better suited to exploring different regions. Most of the 13 days are devoted to city and nature excursions, with the beach stay in Búzios near the end.

### Will there be a Russian-speaking guide in the Pantanal and Bonito?

The itinerary specifies English-speaking guides in those regions. Russian-speaking guiding is provided in Rio and Iguazú.

### Can you choose any travel date?

The Champions Parade at the Sambadrome determines the timing. First align the trip with the Carnival calendar, then arrange flights and accommodation.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. Domestic flights are separately paid services, as are international flights.

## Rio and Iguazú in 7 days: waterfalls, panoramas and tropical islands

This tour lasts **7 days and 6 nights**: travelers spend 4 nights in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and then 2 nights near [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The program combines Rio's two famous mountain viewpoints, a boat outing near islands and the waterfalls on the Brazilian and Argentine sides.

The week-long format suits travelers ready for busy sightseeing days. It has one organized day on the water, but no multi-day resort stay. If you want several days at the beach after the excursions, compare it with the [12-day Búzios itinerary](/brazil/tour/unforgettable-brazil-private-tour-12-days/).

## Rio: why Sugarloaf and Corcovado are visited separately

On day one, guests are met at the airport and transferred to their hotel. Day two includes ascending Sugarloaf via Urca and exploring old Rio. The viewpoints reveal the ocean, Guanabara Bay, city neighborhoods and surrounding mountains.

Day three focuses on Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer. The route to the summit passes through Tijuca Forest. Corcovado's panorama differs from the view from Sugarloaf, showing the coast and city districts from different directions.

The two sightseeing days therefore serve different purposes. One introduces the coastal city and its history; the other focuses on the main mountain viewpoint with the statue. More about the districts and sights appears on our [Rio de Janeiro page](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/).

## Boat trip: Angra dos Reis or Ilha Grande

Day four is spent on the water. After a transfer from the Rio hotel, a **group excursion with an English-speaking guide** and a boat outing are scheduled approximately from 10:00 to 16:00. The area is described as [Angra dos Reis](/brazil/place/angra-dos-reis/) **or** [Ilha Grande](/brazil/place/ilha-grande/).

These are alternatives, so visiting both is not guaranteed in a single day. Angra dos Reis has numerous bays and islands; Ilha Grande is known for wooded slopes and beaches that are readily approached from the water.

The boat excursion replaces city sights with the nature of the Atlantic coast for a day. After returning to Rio, however, the program continues with a flight to the falls the next day: there is no separate resort stay.

## The waterfalls from both sides over two days

Day five includes a domestic flight to Foz do Iguaçu and a visit to the Brazilian side of the falls. Panoramic viewpoints reveal the long series of cascades and forested canyon.

On day six, travelers visit the [Argentine side of Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Walkways let you view waterfalls from different heights and approach individual cascades, including the Devil's Throat area if the route is open. The two national parks have their own visitor rules and protect different portions of one natural system.

Because the excursion requires **crossing an international border**, document requirements must be checked for each traveler's nationality. Weather and water levels may limit access to particular walkways. This is not a reason to omit one of the two sides, but it matters when choosing the season.

Optional activities at Iguazú include a Macuco Safari boat trip and Bird Park. These cost extra. If time is limited, the main priority remains the viewpoints included in the program.

## Flights, guiding and included services

Day seven includes an airport transfer for a flight to São Paulo and the connection home. Within one week, travelers must account for domestic flight segments, airport transfers and connections before an international departure.

**Included** are accommodation at the selected hotels, excursions with an English-speaking guide, entrance tickets and transfers with a driver. **Excluded** are international and domestic flights, optional excursions, food and drinks during transfers.

An important point for Russian-speaking travelers: the approved program specifies an English-speaking guide. Russian-language assistance must not be assumed included. Hotels may be replaced with others of a similar category, and the excursion sequence may be adjusted while preserving the program.

## Who will enjoy this week-long trip?

| Feature | Program |
|---|---|
| Duration | 7 days |
| Nights | Rio — 4, Iguazú — 2 |
| Sea | 1 excursion day |
| Waterfalls | Both sides |
| Guide | English-speaking |

The main advantage is the variety of experiences in one week. The trade-off is intensity: instead of several days by the beach, travelers move from city viewpoints to a boat, then waterfalls and flights. If you prefer a slower trip, explore [other Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) or the [12-day Búzios itinerary](/brazil/tour/unforgettable-brazil-private-tour-12-days/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Rio–Iguazú trip

### Can you see both sides of the falls in a week?

Yes. Day five covers the Brazilian side and day six the Argentine side.

### Do you visit Angra dos Reis and Ilha Grande together?

There is no such guarantee. The program offers a boat day in either the Angra dos Reis or Ilha Grande area, so one of the two options.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. Domestic flights, like the international journey, are among the expenses excluded from the tour price.

### What language are the excursions conducted in?

The published program specifies an English-speaking guide. Another guiding language must be arranged separately.

### Does the tour work as a beach holiday?

There is a boat excursion, but not several free days at a resort. For an extended ocean holiday, a route including Búzios is more suitable.

## São Paulo, Manaus, Rio and Iguazú: a grand Brazil journey in 12 days

Over **12 days**, this itinerary combines four regions that reveal different sides of Brazil. First comes urban [São Paulo](/brazil/place/sao-paulo/), followed by the Amazon via Manaus, then [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) on the Atlantic and finally [Iguazú Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) on both sides of the border.

The tour suits travelers ready for several domestic flights in exchange for a broad variety of experiences. There is no lengthy beach break at the end: its main purpose is exploring four contrasting parts of the country, with a few consecutive days in each.

## How the days are divided

| Days | Region |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | São Paulo |
| 3–4 | Manaus and the Amazon |
| 5–7 | Rio de Janeiro |
| 8–10 | Both sides of Iguazú |
| 11–12 | Return to São Paulo |

**São Paulo** opens the journey. This major city has its own architecture and historic districts. The first two days let travelers explore an urban center before heading to natural regions. Private excursions with a Russian-speaking guide are provided here.

**Manaus and the Amazon** form the next stage. After a domestic flight, travelers move on to river outings and tropical nature. Activities in the Manaus region take place in a group with an English-speaking guide, so the format changes from the preceding city excursions.

**Rio** begins on day five. Plans include Sugarloaf Mountain, historic neighborhoods, Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer. Several days are dedicated to the city, allowing different panoramas without packing both major viewpoint excursions into one overly busy day.

**Iguazú** follows another flight. First comes the Brazilian side of the falls, then the Argentine side. The second excursion requires crossing the border even though the primary destination country for the tour is Brazil. The return to São Paulo is planned for day eleven, and day twelve concludes the trip.

## Why the order of regions matters

São Paulo and Rio are large cities but offer different experiences. São Paulo introduces life in a modern metropolis, while Rio provides mountain and ocean panoramas. The Amazon adds forests, rivers and life along the water; at Iguazú, the main attractions are the cascades, viewpoints and national parks.

Moving between regions requires flights, and a travel day is not the same as a full excursion day. That is why the day-by-day program matters more than simply seeing four geographical names in the title.

For a trip taking in only Rio, the Amazon and Iguazú, consider the [8-day itinerary](/brazil/tour/rio-de-janeiro-amazon-iguazu-falls/). It is shorter and does not include a separate sightseeing stage in São Paulo.

## Guides, transfers and inclusions

The price covers hotel accommodation with breakfast, transfers with a driver and scheduled excursions. **In São Paulo, Rio and Iguazú**, the excursions are **private with a Russian-speaking guide**. **In Manaus**, they are **group outings with an English-speaking guide**.

This distinction is important when choosing the guiding format. Having a Russian-speaking guide in Rio does not imply the same service on the Amazon leg.

International and domestic flights **are excluded**, as are insurance, tips, personal expenses and additional excursions. When arriving in Manaus **after 16:00** or departing **before 14:30**, private transfers are charged extra. Flight times therefore directly affect both the budget and convenience of the trip.

The tour price is **$4323**, but comparing itineraries also requires allowing for several domestic flight tickets and any additional transfers.

## Choosing between a shorter and larger itinerary

This extended tour suits travelers wanting to add **São Paulo** to the classic combination of Rio, the Amazon and Iguazú. It provides another city stage and more time in different regions but requires comfort with extensive travel.

If beach relaxation matters more than the number of regions, see [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) with seaside stays. If tropical nature is your main interest, compare the country's [nature itineraries](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/), focusing on the actual number of days in the forest rather than merely the word Amazon in a title.

## Frequently asked questions about the four-region tour

### How long does the program last?

12 days. It begins and ends in São Paulo and passes through Manaus, Rio and Iguazú in between.

### Are all excursions private?

No. Private Russian-language guiding is provided in São Paulo, Rio and Iguazú; Manaus excursions are shared with an English-speaking guide.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. Domestic flights are paid separately.

### Are there extra expenses for particular Manaus flight times?

Yes. Private transfers are charged separately for arrivals after 16:00 and departures before 14:30.

### Is the Argentine side of Iguazú visited?

Yes. The program includes a separate day on the Argentine side of the falls.

## Brazil from São Paulo to Búzios: why choose this 12-day route?

The journey starts in [São Paulo](/brazil/place/sao-paulo/), continues through [Iguazú](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), and ends with a beach stay in [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/). **Twelve days and eleven nights** introduce contrasting sides of the country: a major metropolis, a natural national park, an oceanfront city and a resort peninsula.

Unlike short sightseeing tours, several days are allocated to Búzios. This suits travelers who want to see the main attractions and then relax by the sea. Excursions are private, with a Russian-speaking guide in São Paulo, Iguazú and Rio.

## São Paulo: the urban start of the trip

Days one and two take place in São Paulo. The sightseeing program covers the historic center, market, theater, central streets and the Avenida Paulista area. Modern architecture and parks introduce the city as a major cultural and business center, rather than just a transfer airport.

This stage differs from the rest of the journey in both experience and pace. For travelers interested in contemporary Brazil, it is a valuable addition to beaches and waterfalls. If your holiday time is limited, compare it with the [Rio–Iguazú express tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-iguazu-express/), which does not include a full São Paulo sightseeing stage.

## Iguazú Falls from both sides of the border

Day three includes a flight to Iguazú and a visit to the Brazilian side of the falls. The broad front of cascades and the surrounding tropical forest are clearly visible here. Day four focuses on the Argentine side, in the [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) area: walking paths and bridges bring visitors closer to individual cascades and provide different perspectives.

Although Brazil is the tour's main destination country, **the Argentine side is included in the route**. This means crossing an actual international border. Check entry requirements for your nationality, travel documents and permission to enter Argentina. The waterfalls are natural attractions, and particular viewpoints may be temporarily closed because of weather or technical conditions.

## Rio and Búzios: sightseeing gives way to relaxation

After Iguazú, the itinerary returns to Rio. The city program includes Sugarloaf Mountain, the old center and Corcovado with Christ the Redeemer. These visits are spread across separate days, so travelers do not have to combine every major Rio viewpoint with a flight on the same day.

Next, travelers head to the Búzios peninsula. Free days here can be spent on beaches, walking around small bays and relaxing. The resort has both calmer beaches and areas for active water sports; the best choice depends on weather and sea conditions.

For travelers primarily seeking the coastline, our [Brazil beach tours selection](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/brazil/) offers other options. In this itinerary, the seaside stage complements a substantial sightseeing route.

## Price and exclusions

The starting tour price is **$4687**. Included are accommodation with breakfast, transfers with a driver and private excursions with Russian-speaking guides in the specified cities. **Domestic and international flights** are paid separately, as are insurance, tips and personal expenses.

When comparing budgets, allow not only for the base price but also for the flights between São Paulo, Iguazú and Rio, plus overland transfers. This itinerary combines two major cities, the falls and a beach finale, without an included flight from Russia or another departure country.

## Frequently asked questions about the São Paulo–Búzios tour

### Is there a separate day on the Argentine side of Iguazú?

Yes. Day four is devoted to exploring the falls from Argentina.

### Are the excursions shared or private?

The program includes private excursions with Russian-speaking guides in São Paulo, Iguazú and Rio.

### Are flights within Brazil included?

No. Domestic flight tickets are listed among additional expenses.

### How many days are allocated to beaches?

After the transfer from Rio to Búzios, the itinerary includes free days at the resort before the return via São Paulo.
